fact: Barnacles are little animals related to crabs, lobsters and shrimps.
There are more than 1,400 kinds of barnacles in the world.
The biggest fish in the ocean is the whale shark.
Whale sharks may grow up to 40 feet long.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.
Some sea creatures make their own light, just like fireflies do.
Glowing creatures live all through the ocean, from the surface to the deep seafloor.
The bowhead whale may live more than 200 years!
Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps.
Dolphins are mammals, not fish. They breathe air with lungs.
Dolphins have to swim up to the surface often to take a breath.
People can't drink seawater. It has far too much salt.
Most fish rest, but they don't sleep the same way people do.
The Pacific sand lance rests by burrowing into the sand.
The glass sponge is a deep-sea animal named for its glass-like skeleton.
Green sea turtles are named for their greenish fat, not their shells.
Grown-up green sea turtles eat only plants, like seagrass and algae.
Scientists think Greenland sharks live at least 250 years.
Horseshoe crabs aren't really crabs. They are closer cousins of spiders and scorpions.
There is really just one big global ocean. It covers 71 percent of Earth.
Most icebergs look white, but some are blue or even green.
Jellyfish are about 95 percent water.
Kelp can grow up to 18 inches in one day.
Like trees in a forest, giant kelp gives food and shelter to many sea animals.
The world's largest waterfall is under the ocean, in the Denmark Strait.
The leatherback is the biggest sea turtle. It can weigh up to 2,000 pounds.
Leatherback sea turtles don't have a hard shell.
Marine snow is a shower of tiny bits that drifts down to the deep sea.
Some flakes of marine snow fall for weeks before they reach the ocean floor.
A nautilus is a cousin of squids and octopuses that lives inside a hard shell.
The ocean looks blue because water soaks up the red colors of sunlight.
On average, the ocean is about 12,080 feet deep.
Seawater freezes at about 28 degrees Fahrenheit, colder than fresh water.
When seawater freezes, the ice has very little salt in it.
Some corals can live for up to 5,000 years.
Penguins have wings, but they use them to swim instead of fly.
Penguins can swim underwater at 15 to 25 miles per hour.
The word plankton comes from a Greek word that means drifter.
Ocean salt comes mostly from rocks on land and from openings in the seafloor.
Sea cucumbers are animals, not vegetables.
Some seaweeds are so tiny you need a microscope to see them.
Most sharks are not dangerous to people. People are not their natural food.
The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of Earth's five ocean basins.
Sponges are simple animals that live in the water.
The best time to explore tide pools is at low tide.
Baby sea turtles hatch together and hurry to the sea all at once.
Whales make sounds to talk, to find food, and to find each other.
Whales travel together in groups called pods.
Christmas tree worms live on coral reefs and are about 1.5 inches long.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth.
The Great Barrier Reef stretches for 1,429 miles.
The highest tides in the world are in Canada, in the Bay of Fundy.
Some beach sand is made by parrotfish. It's parrotfish poop!
A giant bumphead parrotfish can live to be 40 years old.
Point Nemo is the spot in the ocean that is farthest from land.
The longest mountain range on Earth is under the sea. It's called the mid-ocean ridge.
Brain corals don't have brains, but they can grow six feet tall.
Brain corals can live for up to 900 years.
For most sea turtles, the warmth of the sand decides if a baby is a boy or a girl.
Sea lions bark loudly and can walk on land using their big flippers.
Starfish, also called sea stars, are not fish.
There are about 2,000 kinds of sea stars.
Some sea stars have 10, 20, or even 40 arms!
A sunflower sea star moves on 15,000 tiny tube feet.
Hard corals release their eggs all at the same time. It's one of nature's most amazing events.
The Sun is about 100 times wider than Earth.
The Sun is the only star in our solar system.
The Sun is about 93 million miles away from Earth.
Our Sun is a star that is about 4.5 billion years old.
Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system.
Mercury is the fastest planet. It goes around the Sun every 88 Earth days.
If Earth were the size of a nickel, Mercury would be about as big as a blueberry.
Mercury is closest to the Sun, but Venus is the hottest planet.
Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system.
Venus spins the opposite way from most planets.
After the Sun and Moon, Venus is the brightest thing in the sky.
Earth is the only planet in our solar system with liquid water on its surface.
The name Earth comes from Old English. It simply means the ground.
Earth is the only planet in our solar system with just one moon.
About 30 Earth-sized planets could fit between Earth and the Moon.
Put a green pea next to a nickel. That's how big the Moon is next to Earth.
We always see the same side of the Moon from Earth.
The Moon is the only place beyond Earth that people have visited.
If Earth were the size of a nickel, Mars would be about as big as a raspberry.
A day on Mars is just a little longer than a day on Earth.
A day on Mars is called a sol.
A year on Mars lasts 687 Earth days.
Mars has ice caps, old volcanoes and canyons.
If Earth were the size of a grape, Jupiter would be about as big as a basketball.
Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet: just under 10 hours.
Jupiter is 11 times wider than Earth.
Saturn could float in a bathtub, if there were one big enough!
A day on Saturn lasts only about 10 and a half hours.
Saturn is the second-largest planet in our solar system.
Other planets have rings too, but none are as amazing as Saturn's.
Uranus spins on its side, like a rolling ball.
A year on Uranus lasts about 84 Earth years.
Uranus has 28 known moons, named for characters in famous old plays and poems.
Neptune is the only planet you can't see without a telescope.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.
If Earth were the size of a nickel, Neptune would be about as big as a baseball.
Neptune is more than 30 times as far from the Sun as Earth is.
Pluto has five known moons. The biggest one is called Charon.
One day on Pluto lasts about 153 hours.
Sunlight takes about five and a half hours to reach Pluto.
The hottest air temperature ever recorded in Death Valley was 134°F, in 1913.
Death Valley holds the record for the hottest place on Earth.
Yellowstone has more than 10,000 hot springs, geysers and other hot spots.
More than 500 of Yellowstone's hot features are geysers.
Old Faithful geyser shoots water about 130 feet high on average.
The General Grant Tree in Kings Canyon National Park is the world's second-largest tree.
source: National Park Service, Sequoia & Kings Canyon
